Author one golden eval task for the design's section 5 format (the spec file, the starting repo, a hidden test and a known-good solution). The task: A function toJob(ticket, inSet) builds a job object { id, title } from a ticket { id, title, dependsOn } and must add an after list holding only the dependencies that are in inSet (a Set of ids), and must leave the after field out completely when that list would be empty, because the manifest validator rejects an empty after. The starting file always sets after, even when empty, and keeps dependencies that are not in the set. Real lesson: the ticket manifest builder emitted an empty after and the validator rejected the manifest. The eval id is ticket-after-empty. The spec has tags (2 to 4), title, a prompt for the worker under test (state the contract of toJob clearly in 3 to 8 sentences; do not mention the hidden test, and do not reveal the lesson), context listing the module path inside the starting repo, outputs listing the same module path, check argv node --test followed by the hidden test path inside the repo layout (the hidden folder is copied over the repo, so the hidden test path is test/<name>.test.mjs). The starting repo has only the buggy or empty module (an ES module file; no package.json) exporting toJob. The hidden test has at least 8 assertions covering normal cases, edge cases and the real failure. The solution is the corrected module and must pass the hidden test; the starting module must fail it. Make the hidden test deterministic and quick (under 2 seconds), using only node built-ins, and clean up temp folders it creates.

Author one golden eval task for the design's section 5 format (the spec file, the starting repo, a hidden test and a known-good solution). The task: An async function withLock(file, fn, options) takes an exclusive lock by creating the lock file with the exclusive flag, runs fn, and always removes the lock afterwards, also when fn throws. When the lock file already exists and is younger than options.staleMs (default 600000) it must reject with an error whose code is 'busy' without running fn; when it is older it must take it over and run fn. The starting file never removes the lock when fn throws and never takes over a stale one. Real lesson: go --scope needed one wave at a time with a stale-lock takeover. The eval id is stale-lock.
